Q5290784.label: 1942 Dominican Republic general election
Q5290784.summary: General elections were held in the Dominican Republic on 16 May 1942. Rafael Trujillo, who had previously served as president from 1930 to 1938, was the sole presidential candidate and was returned to office unopposed. He had remained the country's de facto leader even after leaving office for the first time. His Dominican Party won every seat in the Congressional elections.

Q800.label: Costa Rica
Q800.summary: Costa Rica, officially the Republic of Costa Rica, is a country in Central America. It borders Nicaragua to the north, the Caribbean Sea to the northeast, Panama to the southeast, and the Pacific Ocean to the southwest, sharing a maritime border with Ecuador to the south of Cocos Island. It has a population of around five million in a land area of nearly 51,180 km2 (19,760 sq mi); the capital and largest city is San José, home to around 350,000 residents and two million people in the surrounding metropolitan area.

Q110534944.label: 2022 Hungarian LGBTQ rights referendum
Q110534944.summary: A referendum was held in Hungary on 3 April 2022, coinciding with the parliamentary elections. While the overwhelming majority of valid votes were cast as "no" to the four referendum questions, the share of valid votes was below the 50% required for the result to be considered valid and thus the referendum was rejected.

Q2700064.label: 1997 Albanian parliamentary election
Q2700064.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in Albania on 29 June 1997 alongside a simultaneous referendum on restoring the monarchy, with a second round of voting for 32 seats on 6 July. The elections were called as a response to the 1997 Albanian civil unrest.

Q1264416.label: 1992 Croatian presidential election
Q1264416.summary: Presidential elections were held in Croatia for the first time on 2 August 1992 alongside simultaneous parliamentary elections. The result was a victory for incumbent Franjo Tuđman of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), who received 58% of the vote, becoming the first popularly elected president of Croatia. Voter turnout was 75%.

Q59978016.label: Rosen Zhelyazkov
Q59978016.summary: Rosen Dimitrov Zhelyazkov is a Bulgarian politician who served as Prime Minister of Bulgaria from 2025 to 2026. He previously served as Minister of Transport from 2018 to 2021, Member of the National Assembly from 2021 to 2025, and Speaker of the National Assembly from 2023 to 2024. He is a member of the conservative GERB party.

Q2634016.label: 2004 Belarusian referendum
Q2634016.summary: A referendum on allowing President Lukashenko to stand in further elections was held in Belarus on 17 October 2004, alongside parliamentary elections. Lukashenko was nearing the end of his constitutionally-limited two terms, and the change would allow him to run for a third term.

Q7855392.label: 1989 Turkish presidential election
Q7855392.summary: The 1989 Turkish presidential election refers the election to choose the country's eighth president, to succeed Kenan Evren. The candidate of the governing Motherland Party (ANAP) was its leader and Prime Minister Turgut Özal. In the first and second rounds, the ruling party ANAP was unsuccessful in electing its candidate.

Q3636512.label: Battle of Lwów
Q3636512.desc: Lwów besieged by Germany during the Invasion of Poland of 1939 at the outbreak of World War II
Q3636512.summary: The Battle of Lwów was a World War II battle for the control over the formerly Polish city of Lwów between the Polish Army and the invading Wehrmacht and the Red Army. The city was seen as the key to the so-called Romanian Bridgehead and was defended at all costs.

Q1200928.label: Japanese invasion of Thailand
Q1200928.summary: The Japanese invasion of Thailand occurred on 8 December 1941. It was briefly fought between the Kingdom of Thailand and the Empire of Japan. Despite fierce fighting in southern Thailand, the fighting lasted only five hours before ending in a ceasefire. Thailand and Japan then formed an alliance making Thailand part of the Axis alliance until the end of World War II. It occurred roughly two hours before the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.

Q153376.label: Second Battle of El Alamein
Q153376.desc: 1942 major turning point in the Western Desert Campaign of the Second World War
Q153376.img: Lieutenant General Bernard Montgomery, commanding the British Eighth Army in North Africa, in the turret of his Grant command tank at El Alamein, 5 November 1942. E18980.jpg
Q153376.summary: The Second Battle of El Alamein was a battle of the Second World War that took place near the Egyptian railway halt of El Alamein. The First Battle of El Alamein and the Battle of Alam el Halfa had prevented the Axis from advancing further into Egypt.

Q16898848.label: Battle of the Punchbowl
Q16898848.img: Punchbowl, Heartbreak Ridge and Bloody Ridge.gif
Q16898848.summary: The Battle of the Punchbowl, was one of the last battles of the movement phase of the Korean War. Following the breakdown of armistice negotiations in August 1951, the United Nations Command (UN) decided to launch a limited offensive in the late summer/early autumn to shorten and straighten sections of their lines, acquire better defensive terrain, and deny the enemy key vantage points from which they could observe and target UN positions.

Q2026272.label: Operation Phantom Thunder
Q2026272.img: American soldier during firefight in Adhamiyah, Baghdad (Operation Phantom Thunder).jpg
Q2026272.summary: Operation Phantom Thunder began on 16 June 2007, when Multi-National Force-Iraq launched major offensive operations against al-Qaeda and other extremist terrorists operating throughout Iraq. It was the largest coordinated military operation since the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

Q29017888.label: 2017 Russian Air Force Al-Bab incident
Q29017888.img: Tupolev Tu-22M3 Backfire, Russia - Air Force JP7618917.jpg
Q29017888.summary: The 2017 Russian Air Force Al-Bab incident occurred when three Turkish soldiers were killed and 11 injured after a Russian Air Force Tupolev Tu-22M attacked Turkish soldiers accidentally during Operation Spring Shield in al-Bab, Syria.

Q114350880.label: Battle of Lyman
Q114350880.desc: September to October 2022 battle in Ukraine
Q114350880.wiki: Lyman front of the 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive
Q114350880.img: Fallen Russian soldiers during the retreat from Lyman.jpg
Q114350880.summary: In September 2022, a military engagement took place near Lyman, Ukraine, during a major Ukrainian counteroffensive in Kharkiv Oblast. By 30 September, Ukrainian forces had closed in on the city after crossing the Siverskyi Donets River, advancing along Lyman's southern and eastern flanks while capturing land northwest of the settlement, allowing Ukrainian forces to cut off the only road left supplying the occupying forces from the north. On 1 October, Ukrainian forces entered Lyman after a Russian withdrawal.

mentions.c: Part of Russian invasion of Ukraine

Q130552096.label: October 2024 Rufaida school attack
Q130552096.summary: On 10 October 2024, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) bombed Rufaida school-turned-shelter in Deir al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip. The airstrikes killed at least 28 Palestinians and injured more than 54. The IDF did not issue a warning before striking the building, which was sheltering 1,000 people that were displaced by the Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip. The IDF said it have struck "command post used by terror operatives within the compound."
